newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi billionaire Prince Al-Waleed buys TWA stake.
newsitem.headline: Saudi billionaire Prince Al-Waleed buys TWA stake.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's billionaire Prince Al-Waleed bin Talal, whose global business empire includes stakes in banks, luxury hotels and a fun park, said on Wednesday he has purchased five percent of stock in Trans World Airlines Inc.

A statement from the prince's office in the Saudi capital Riyadh said "he has purchased five percent of the outstanding common stock of Trans World Airlines, Inc (TWA) for investment purposes". It did not give a value for the deal.
TWA is the United States' seventh largest air carrier.
The statement said the purchase was the first in the airline industry by the prince, who has also been touted as the possible white knight for bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker.
It described the deal as a new investment trend by the prince, a nephew of Saudi Arabia's King Fahd.
TWA on Tuesday reported a wider-than-expected net loss for the fourth quarter of 1996 of $258.6 million or $5.56 a share, compared to a loss of $27.8 million or $0.84 a share a year earlier.
TWA 's shares were last quoted at $6-7/8.

The prince, who calls a palace in Riyadh home, has built a multi-billion dollar business empire with interests in construction, real estate, banking, travel, broadcast media, supermarkets and other sectors.
His worldwide investments include shares in U.S. banking giant Citicorp and Euro Disney as well as international hotels like the famed Hotel George V in Paris and the Plaza Hotel in New York.
His portfolio also includes stakes in the Four Season's and Fairmont Hotel chains.
The prince, who heads the United Saudi Commercial Bank, has also made substantial investments in Canary Wharf in London's Docklands and U.S. upmarket retail group Saks Fifth Avenue.
He has also set up Kingdom Entertainment with U.S. popstar Michael Jackson.
The statement from Prince Al-Waleed's Riyadh office did not give any other details.
